clauses.reason: Executive Order 10634, signed 1955-08-25 (20 FR 6433), provides under the Defense Production Act of 1950 that, whenever financial assistance is not otherwise available on reasonable terms, loans (including participations and guarantees) under section 302 of that Act may be made to aid the reconstruction, rehabilitation or replacement of facilities destroyed or damaged by a major disaster, when the facilities are required for national defense as determined by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization. No own-terms sunset or condition ends it. Later events, each a change to the determining officer and not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments): (1) Executive Order 10773, signed 1958-07-01 (23 FR 5061). Section 3(a) provides that each reference in any prior Executive order to the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization is hereby "amended to refer to the Director of the" Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization. Before: the determination was made by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization; after: by the Director of the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization. The held Federal Register text covers only the order's first two printed pages (23 FR 5061-5062); the list in section 4(b) that names EO 10634 as item (14), and section 10, which makes the order effective as of July 1, 1958, are on the following page and are seen only in the American Presidency Project transcription, which is not a cited source. July 1, 1958 is also the signing date, so the date does not depend on that page. (2) Executive Order 11051, signed 1962-09-27 (27 FR 9683), section 601, which states that each reference to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization or to its Director in the listed orders is amended to refer to the Office of Emergency Planning and its Director; the list includes, as the OCR prints it, "E xecu tive O rder N o. 10634 o f August 25,1955". Before: the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization; after: the Director of the Office of Emergency Planning. EO 11051 has no effective-date wording, so its signing date is recorded. (3) Executive Order 11725, signed 1973-06-27 (38 FR 17175), section 3, which transfers to the Administrator of General Services all authority vested in the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness as of June 30, 1973, including functions under "(7 ) Executive Order No. 10634 of August 25, 1955, relating to loans" for defense facilities damaged by a major disaster; section 8 states "This order shall be effective as of July 1, 1973." Before: the determination rested with the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness; after: the authority rested with the Administrator of General Services. EO 11725 prints no replacement text for EO 10634. First end: Executive Order 12148, Federal Emergency Management, section 5-106: "Executive Order No. 10634, as amended, relating to loans for facilities" destroyed or damaged by a major disaster, is revoked. Its closing section states "This Order is effective July 15,1979." EO 12148 was signed 1979-07-20, so the stated effective date is retroactive; the first end is recorded on the stated effective date, 1979-07-15, and the signing date 1979-07-20 is the alternative reading. No held source shows an earlier lapse of the section 302 authority the order invokes.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10634 (20 FR 6433, Federal Register of September 1, 1955), signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower and dated August 25, 1955; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: one whole-order clause. Under the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, the order provides that, whenever financial assistance is not otherwise available on reasonable terms, loans (including participations in, or guarantees of, loans) under section 302 of that Act may be made to aid the reconstruction, rehabilitation or replacement of facilities destroyed or damaged by a major disaster, whenever the facilities are required for national defense as determined by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization. Later events (strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21, each recorded with date, actor, mechanism and before and after text): EO 10773 (effective July 1, 1958) amends every reference in prior orders to the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization to refer to the Director of the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization; EO 11051 section 601 (1962-09-27) amends the references in this order to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization and its Director to refer to the Office of Emergency Planning and its Director; EO 11725 section 3 (effective July 1, 1973) transfers the authority then vested in the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness under this order to the Administrator of General Services. None of them revokes or terminates the order. Ending: EO 12148 section 5-106 revokes the order, effective July 15, 1979 by that order's own effective-date sentence (signed July 20, 1979). Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code search has two hits, a note under 42 U.S.C. 5195 reprinting EO 12148 with its section 5-106 revocation and the title 50 disposition table listing this order as omitted; the eCFR search has two hits for which the dossier holds no located text, so they were not relied on either way; the Federal Register catalog notes (five machine hits) record the amendments by EO 10773 and EO 11051, a cross-reference to EO 11725 and the revocation by EO 12148.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The order has no sunset or condition ending it. (2) EO 10773, EO 11051 and EO 11725 change which officer makes the national-defense determination or holds the authority; each is recorded as a later event, and none revokes or terminates the order. (3) The intervening statutory renamings of the mobilization office (from the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization, and from the Office of Emergency Planning to the Office of Emergency Preparedness) are not shown by any held source and do not name the order, so they are not recorded as events or ends. (4) No held source shows that the section 302 loan authority lapsed before 1979; that possibility is not excluded, but it is not supported by held evidence, and the order is permissive, so it is not treated as ended by disuse. (5) EO 12148 names the order and revokes it, effective July 15, 1979.","independent_command_check":"The loan authority itself is conferred by section 302 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, which the order invokes and which is not held in this packet. The order adds only the permission to use that authority for major-disaster facilities that the named officer determines are required for national defense; it creates no separate continuing command.","savings_check":"No savings wording in EO 12148 attaches to the revocation; loans already made are past transactions governed by their own terms and the statute.","scope_check":"One clause covers the whole order. EO 12148 section 5-106 revokes the order, as amended, without exception, so the whole order ends on that date."}

savings.reason: EO 12148 attaches no savings sentence to the section 5-106 revocation, and the held text contains no general savings clause (searched for saving, remain in, continue in, nothing in and notwithstanding). Loans already made would be governed by their own terms and by section 302 of the Defense Production Act, not by this order; no continuing right or duty arising only from the order is shown.
